content.title: What are Variables and Data Types?
content.description: Variables are named memory locations used to store data, while data types define the kind of data a variable can hold and the operations that can be performed on it.

content.content: Every Java program works with data. Before storing any value, Java requires you to declare a variable along with its data type. The data type determines the size of memory allocated, the range of values, and the operations that can be performed on the variable.

content.title: Why Variables Matter
content.content: Variables allow programs to store, retrieve, and manipulate data efficiently during execution.

content.title: Variable Creation Process
steps: Use the Variable in the Program

content.content: A variable declaration specifies both the data type and the variable name. Variables can be initialized during declaration or later in the program.

content.title: Variable Declaration

content.content: Primitive data types are predefined by Java and store simple values directly in memory.

content.title: Primitive Types
content.description: Java provides eight primitive data types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, and boolean.

content.content: Non-primitive (reference) data types store references to objects rather than actual values. Examples include String, Arrays, Classes, and Interfaces.

content.title: Did You Know?
content.content: Strings are not primitive data types in Java. They are objects of the String class.
Starting from Java 10, local variables can be declared using the var keyword. The compiler automatically infers the data type based on the assigned value.

content.title: Using var

content.content: Java follows specific rules and conventions for naming variables to improve readability and maintainability.

items.question: Can a variable start with a number?
items.answer: No. Variable names cannot begin with digits.

items.question: Can keywords be used as variable names?
items.answer: No. Reserved keywords like int, class, and public cannot be used.

items.question: What naming convention is recommended?
items.answer: Use camelCase for variable names, such as studentName or totalMarks.

content.title: Labeled Storage Boxes
content.content: Imagine different storage boxes labeled for books, clothes, or electronics. You place only the appropriate item inside each box. Similarly, a data type determines what kind of value a variable can store.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers frequently ask about primitive data types, memory size, default values, variable naming rules, and the difference between primitive and reference types.

items.question: Why does assigning 12.5 to an int cause an error?
items.answer: Because int stores only whole numbers.

items.question: Why must float values end with 'f'?
items.answer: Without 'f', decimal values are treated as double by default.

items.question: Why can't variables have duplicate names in the same scope?
items.answer: Each variable name must uniquely identify a memory location within its scope.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Always choose the smallest appropriate data type to improve memory efficiency while maintaining readability.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Every variable has a data type.
Java has eight primitive data types.
String is a reference type, not a primitive type.
Use meaningful variable names following camelCase.
